facts.topic: Ordinary StartGame initializes the base HUD request screen
facts.contract: The matched StartGame path assigns ItemStackNetManagerClient to the player before calling onClientCreatedLevel. That client callback adds the player to the level; Level::addUser invokes initHUDContainerManager, whose LocalPlayer target obtains the HUD model and calls postInit. postInit opens an item-stack manager screen whenever the manager pointer exists. The recovered opening chain does not gate that operation on mEnabled. This establishes the normal joined-player HUD screen used by a legacy-use scope; it does not establish every exceptional player-creation path.

facts.topic: Screen push, fallback selection, and base-screen lifetime
facts.contract: Opening a screen pushes an entity with ContainerScreenContext and calls the concrete client screen initializer, which creates ClientScreenData. Current-screen lookup first tries the active request-screen weak reference, then falls back to the top screen stack entry. Closing a screen only pops when at least two entries exist, preserving the base screen. No isEnabled gate occurs in the recovered open, current-screen lookup, or close bodies.

facts.topic: Legacy counter is process-global and separate from the active scope
facts.contract: The legacy-ID allocator uses a zero-initialized process-global int32 counter and advances it as min(counter,-2)-2. Its first allocation in a fresh process is -4. A separate typed-ID constructor and the inlined begin-scope path share that counter, so the first ID observed in one session can be later. Opening or ending a scope does not reset the global in the recovered code. Scope cleanup resets the manager active ID to0 and clears its changed-slot map. The scan of direct RIP-relative reads and writes found two allocator bodies, both advancing rather than resetting the counter; this is not an exhaustive indirect-memory-write proof.

facts.topic: Empty consumption and ordinary source fields
facts.contract: In the traced ordinary inventory setter chain, a last-item consumption falls back to FillingContainer because the manager helper rejects an empty proposed stack. The transaction context still records old-to-empty action. That helper does not register the empty slot, and outgoing legacy decoration becomes0 when the collected slot vector is empty. The change callback initializes InventorySource type0, container0 for main inventory or119 for offhand, and memory flags0; main slot is the supplied selected slot, offhand slot0. Instabuild skips the native consumption decrement, so this chain has no count-change action when the stack remains unchanged. Dynamic event listeners were not exhaustively enumerated; the empty-slot conclusion is bounded to the recovered ordinary setter/callback path.

facts.topic: Server records legacy IDs by supported player container and slot
facts.contract: The matched integrated-server legacy-request helper accepts only negative even IDs below -1. It recognizes InventoryContainer29, ArmorContainer6 and OffhandContainer34. For listed in-range slots whose current stack has the server-ID alternative, it records the supplied legacy ID and current server stack ID in the corresponding player container slot mapping. The recovered helper itself does not construct or send ItemStackResponse. This evidence describes the bundled server implementation, not every custom server.

facts.topic: A later request can refer to a predicted legacy stack ID
facts.contract: The request-slot validator distinguishes server-ID variant0, ordinary client-request variant1 and legacy variant2. For legacy variant2, it requires a negative even ID below -1, finds the corresponding supported player container by runtime ID, bounds-checks the requested slot, requires that slot stored exactly that legacy ID, then uses the paired server stack ID. Thus a surviving predicted stack can be referenced before receiving a new positive server ID, but an unrelated or stale legacy ID does not pass this mapping lookup.

facts.topic: Ordinary ItemStackResponse does not acknowledge the legacy-ID family
facts.contract: The client ItemStackResponse consumer loops over responses and accepts only negative odd request IDs at its initial request-ID gate. Other IDs enter an invalid-ID diagnostic path and are skipped before normal lookup/correction handling. Negative even legacy IDs therefore must not be put into the ordinary odd-request response or rollback queue. Further validation and missing-request behavior remain separate conditions.

facts.topic: Incoming InventorySlot replaces the main inventory stack without a legacy ack wait
facts.contract: For main inventory container0 and an in-range slot, the client decodes the incoming descriptor to ItemStack, records the old-to-new pending action, then invokes Inventory::setItemWithForceBalance with forceBalance=false. No legacy request-ID match or acknowledgement gate appears before this replacement in the recovered path. This provides the ordinary server slot correction path; the full behavior of every sparse/custom container and concurrent ordinary request is outside this conclusion.

facts.topic: Net-ID decoding uses sign and parity to select its variant
facts.contract: ItemStackNetIdVariant::deserialize peeks a signed VarInt and restores the stream cursor before decoding the selected typed alternative. Nonnegative values choose server IDs, negative odd values choose ordinary client request IDs, and negative even values choose legacy request IDs. This establishes the raw ID-family selection; it is not a complete proof of ItemV4 optional presence or every descriptor serialization option.

facts.contract: The matched Item constructor initializes mMaxStackSize to64. The verified Item and ComponentItem vtables both resolve getMaxStackSize to a leaf returning that byte. This supports using64 when a component item definition has no max_stack_size override, but a specific wind-charge definition is an external asset fact rather than a value recovered from this executable.

facts.topic: Client ItemUse descriptors omit net IDs on the matched cereal wire path
facts.contract: The ordinary client baseUseItem path captures its held descriptor before item use, and builds action old/new descriptors from their corresponding stack snapshots. Their ItemStack constructor copies the net-ID variant but initializes mIncludeNetIds=false. The packet Transaction property getter enables new-action descriptor IDs only for a server-side payload; the client branch skips that loop. The actual mode5 NetworkItemStackDescriptor conversion creates its optional Net Id Variant only when mIncludeNetIds is true. The optional writer emits its presence Boolean and only writes the ID when present. Therefore the recovered outgoing client ItemUse held, from-item and to-item descriptors have an absent Net Id Variant, while a surviving locally predicted raw ItemStack may still retain its negative-even legacy ID for later ItemStackRequest references. This conclusion is for this recovered constructor/send path, not arbitrary descriptor producers or other packets.

limits: These code/data-flow facts are from the matched protocol2193 executable and its PDB. No protocol2225 equivalence is implied.
The bundled integrated-server mapping is useful for protocol interpretation; custom servers may implement different authority or reconciliation policies.

The ordinary main-inventory empty-item callback path is established. All ActorGameplayEvent listeners, offhand variants, custom containers, and all interleavings with normal odd stack requests were not exhaustively reconstructed.

The ItemUse descriptor optional-ID rule is closed for the recovered mode5 client send path, but no full byte-for-byte transaction serializer trace is claimed. InventorySource memory flags0 must not be confused with wire optional presence.
The static default64 is independent of external wind-charge asset contents. An asset-version mismatch must remain explicit when using a nearby pinned Mojang sample.

Normal vanilla rule registration contains39 entries and does not register PDB Education rule index40 AllowDestructiveObjects. No Education network key was recovered; it must not be equated to mayFly, immutableWorld or worldBuilder.
This export contains metadata, addresses and bounded conclusions only. It contains no executable, PDB, machine-code bytes, or disassembly.
